new_statements.rule_in_words: Hozo is described as a tone language in which tone distinguishes both lexical items and grammatical forms; no source opened says anything about word stress or its position.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Note that Küspert 2015 fn. 190 'Stress on last vowel.' (p. 63) belongs to the Seze column of the wordlist ('two' nɔmbe), not to Hozo.
new_statements.domain_note: The 2022 statement is a sociolinguistic remark (speakers' uncertainty in 'the correct use of tones'), not a phonological description; no domain (word vs phrase) is specified. The 2015 note is a wordlist footnote covering the whole 'Mao-Komo' group tentatively.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources concern the Hozo/Hoozo of the Begi–Kondala area (autonym Ak'mo Wandi; Küspert 2015 also 'Shuluyo' as a variety/clan name) = hozo1236. Not to be confused with Seze/Sezo (seze1238) or Northern/Bambassi Mao (bamb1262, Ahland 2012). The 'Stress on last vowel' footnote in Küspert 2015 is a Seze datum.

sources.citation: Küspert, Klaus-Christian. 2015. The Mao and Komo Languages in the Begi–Tongo area in Western Ethiopia: Classification, Designations, and Distribution. Linguistic Discovery 13(1): 1–63. DOI 10.1349/ps1.1537-0852.a.447
sources.note: Survey/classification paper with 38/78-item wordlists. No stress statement for Hozo. Footnote 140, p. 60 (Appendix 3 wordlist): 'tone difference; tones may be distinctive in all "Mao-Komo languages", but are not written here because of poor data.' Footnote 190, p. 63, 'Stress on last vowel.' is attached to the Seze column ('two' nɔmbe), not to Hozo (Hozo 'two' is dɔmbɔ in the next column).

sources.citation: Ahland, Michael Bryan. 2012. A Grammar of Northern Mao (Màwés Aas'è). PhD dissertation, University of Oregon. hdl 1794/12456
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Northern Mao (Bambassi), not Hozo. Hozo appears only in comparative pronoun/numeral tables (pp. 240–241, 'Table 5.2') taken from Siebert et al. 1994 and Bender 2000; notes 'Bender does not include tone marking for his pronominal data (2000:183)'. Nothing on Hozo stress or tone.
